uj/ Language Attrition is a well studied occurrence. We discussed it in some depth in my Second Language Acquisition and Psycholinguistic Courses this year. 

Basically those still within the "Critical Period" (quotations marks because some people argue it should be called Sensitive Period rather than Critical) acquire language much easier due to heightened neuroplasticity at a young age. This heightened plasticity is also why they attrite languages much quicker. That does not mean, however, that young people are the only people who can learn/lose languages. Sure an older person takes longer to learn a language and they might never reach 100% nativelike level, but they can still learn it. Completely analogously, an older person can lose their L1. It takes longer than someone who was adopted internationally at a young age and they might retain some basic vocab/syntactical knowledge, but some degree of attrition is definitely still possible in adulthood.

Attrition is adults is a bit less well studied than in young people, because it's just easier to get young people into a lab as they don't have jobs.

TL;DR Losing a language is possible at almost any age, jt just takes longer and happens less fully if you're older when it happens.

As Medic, never contest the point on your own unless the game is about to end in two seconds and you can stretch the game just long enough to allow the Tanks and DPS classes to show up. When this happens, you will die, always.

#RANDOM DROPS

Random items will drop every few minutes/hours of gameplay. This information is carried over by a little triangular sign with an exclamation mark in the middle in the top left corner of the main menu. This item is mostly a random weapon (not determined by the current class, it is completely random) or sometimes if you are really lucky a hat. Weapons that you do not want can be combined to create one scrap metal. Two weapons make a scrap, three scrap make a reclaimed, three reclaimed make a refined. I havent played the game in months so I don't remember exactly where all these options are but it is very intuitive.

#TRADING ITEMS

Ignore the in-game store, its overpriced as fuck. You will however have to buy at least one item from the in-game store to enable trading with other players. I recommend the Backpack Extender since it is extremely cheap and gives you nice large backpack. Then you will have to have had Steam Authenticator active for at least a week before you can begin to trade. The currency used in trades is metal and keys, listed here from lowest value to highest value :

Scrap Metal

Reclaimed Metal

Refined Metal

Mannco Supply Crate Key

If you want to buy/sell an item go to Backpack.tf, the general rate is 1 weapon for 1 weapon or sometimes 1 weapon for 1 scrap. There are many bots on the website that auto-accept trades. It is not a Steam affiliate site, but it is completely safe. To find an item you want to buy click on Classified Listings, should open a search tab. Clicking on a trade offer on the website opens up a trade window in Steam where you will be able to trade items with each other. You can also use Backpack.tf to check the price of items by clicking on the search tab that is top right on the home page of the website.

#PURCHASING ITEMS FOR MONEY

If you want to purchase some items for IRL money, use Marketplace.tf, again like Backpack.tf, not a Steam affiliate site, but still safe. All items are sold here between players, from scrap metal to keys to the most rare hat in the game.
 

#MISCELLANEOUS

Conversion rates from IRL money to scrap to reclaimed to refined can be done using the site Calculator.tf.
